value.body: Law graduates can join government as legal officers in ministries and departments, public-sector undertakings (PSUs), public-sector banks and the armed forces' Judge Advocate General (JAG) branches. The work covers drafting, contracts, managing litigation, legal opinions and compliance.

items.label: PSU law trainees
items.note: Several PSUs shortlist on CLAT-PG, then interview

items.label: JAG commission
items.note: 10 years, extendable by 4; permanent commission possible

value.title: How you get in
value.body: An LLB (three-year or five-year integrated) with eligibility to enrol as an advocate. Routes: PSU law trainee posts (often CLAT-PG based); IBPS SO Law Officer in public-sector banks; UPSC and state PSC notices for legal advisers and prosecutors; and the Army JAG entry (CLAT-PG score, SSB interview and medical).

value.title: At a glance
items: Some posts ask for years of practice at the Bar, so freshers have fewer options.
Each PSU recruits separately; minimum marks and age limits vary.
JAG vacancies are very few in each course.
Judicial service (civil judge) is a separate route through state PSC or High Court exams.
